summary: Flow cytometry of a bone marrow aspirate (viability 94% by 7-AAD; eight-color panel, CD45 vs side scatter gating) shows an abnormal myeloid blast population of approximately 22% of total nucleated cells expressing CD34 (subset, ~60%), CD117, HLA-DR (bright), CD13, CD33 (bright), CD38, CD64, dim CD4 and dim cytoplasmic MPO, with aberrant CD56 (partial) and CD7 (subset); CD14 negative on blasts and CD2/CD19/cyCD3 negative. There is a markedly expanded, left-shifted monocytic compartment (maturing monocytes 19% plus promonocytes/immature monocytic 11%, together approximately 30% of TNC) with bright uniform CD64, CD14 on the maturing fraction, CD11b, CD11c, CD36, HLA-DR and dim CD4. The report states the combined findings are diagnostic of acute myeloid leukemia with monocytic differentiation and that the immunophenotype establishes the monocytic lineage that was only favored on morphology. It notes the flow blast estimate (22%) differs modestly from the manual aspirate differential, that aberrant CD56/CD7 may be useful for MRD tracking, and that correlation with cytogenetic and molecular studies is required for final classification.

stated_limitations: The flow blast estimate (22%) differs modestly from the manual aspirate differential; the report states flow gating and manual counts are expected to differ and either value supports the diagnosis in this context. Correlation with cytogenetic and molecular studies is required for final classification. Flow cytometry is a component study within a combined diagnostic workup; final lineage and classification require integration with morphology, cytogenetics, and molecular results. Method is a laboratory-developed test with performance characteristics established by the performing laboratory.
